blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: CT-to-PET synthesis estimates functional PET images from anatomical CT scans for auxiliary analysis, representation pretraining, and missing-modality completion. Brownian Bridge diffusion models can produce multiple PET candidates of different quality under the same CT condition, exposing an intra-condition quality hierarchy. Candidate quality spans complementary spatial, structural, and intensity dimensions, while DPO-only fine-tuning may compromise absolute synthesis fidelity. We propose MedicalDPO which converts this hierarchy into preference supervision automatically constructed from paired CT-PET training data. Multiple candidates are ranked across the three fidelity dimensions, and strict cross-metric verification retains preferred-rejected pairs with consistent quality separation. Relative denoising-error preference optimization is jointly trained with the original Brownian Bridge objective to anchor the pretrained CT-to-PET mapping, while condition-balanced multi-pair rotation distributes preference supervision across CT conditions. Experiments on BBDM and CPDM show improvements across LPIPS, MAE, SSIM, and PSNR. Further analyses demonstrate metric complementarity and clear pair separation, while ablations show that the original training objective prevents the substantial degradation caused by DPO-only fine-tuning.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: CT-to-PET synthesis aims to estimate functional positron emission tomography (PET) images from anatomical computed tomography (CT) scans [ 16 ] . This cross-modal translation can support auxiliary image analysis, representation pretraining, and missing-modality completion in multimodal medical imaging systems [ 19 , 25 ] . Its practical value depends on whether the synthesized PET images faithfully recover the spatial distribution, structural appearance, and intensity of metabolic uptake [ 25 ] . However, CT primarily describes anatomical structure, whereas PET reflects functional activity that is not fully observable from CT [ 16 ] . This cross-modal information gap makes reliable CT-to-PET synthesis fundamentally challenging.
blocks.zh: CT-对PET合成旨在估算从解剖计算成的成像扫描中得出的功能正元排放成像图(PET)图像[16]. 这种跨模式翻译可以支持辅助图像分析,表现预训,以及多模式医疗成像系统中的缺失模式完成[19,25]. 其实用价值取决于被合成的PET图像是否忠实地恢复了新陈代谢吸收的空间分布,结构外观和强度[25]. 然而,CT主要描述解剖结构,而PET则反映了无法从CT[16]中充分观测到的功能活性. 这种跨模式的信息差距使得可靠的CT到PET综合具有根本的挑战性.

blocks.en:
Diffusion-based image translation models have shown strong potential for CT-to-PET synthesis. Brownian Bridge Diffusion Models
(BBDMs) formulate image translation as a stochastic bridge directly connecting the source and target domains [ 12 ] , while the Conditional PET Diffusion Model (CPDM) incorporates CT-specific attention and attenuation guidance for PET generation [ 16 ] . Despite their promising performance, stochastic generation can produce PET candidates of substantially different quality under the same CT condition [ 12 , 29 ] .
Some candidates accurately recover high-uptake regions and global PET structure, while others exhibit localization errors, missing functional patterns, or intensity deviations. Standard diffusion training optimizes each target sample independently and leaves these relative quality differences among generated candidates unused [ 12 , 16 ] .
This observation leads to two key insights. First, stochastic generation exposes an intra-condition quality hierarchy . Multiple PET samples generated from the same CT provide automatically available preference supervision. A model can therefore learn not only from the ground-truth PET image, but also from the relative quality ordering of its own generated candidates. Second, PET candidate quality forms a vector, not a scalar . Spatial fidelity reflects the localization of uptake regions, intensity fidelity measures the accuracy of tracer uptake values, and structural fidelity characterizes overall PET appearance [ 25 , 11 ] . These dimensions describe complementary properties and may assign different rankings to the same candidate set, as shown in Fig. 1 . These complementary rankings motivate a joint representation of spatial, intensity, and structural fidelity for preference construction.

blocks.en:
Learning from these candidate-level preferences introduces three key challenges.
First, medical preference construction must integrate complementary fidelity dimensions while excluding ambiguous pairs. A candidate favored by one metric may still contain substantial errors in another dimension, making a single-metric preference potentially incomplete [ 11 , 4 ] . Second, Direct
Preference Optimization (DPO) [ 20 ] optimizes relative preference differences but does not explicitly preserve absolute synthesis fidelity. DPO-only fine-tuning may therefore shift the model away from its pretrained CT-to-PET mapping. Third, a single CT condition may produce multiple valid preference pairs. Treating all pairs as independent training samples overweights conditions with more valid combinations, motivating condition-balanced pair selection during optimization.
blocks.zh:
从这些候选人一级的偏好学习,提出了三大挑战。
首先,医疗偏好构建必须结合互补的忠诚层面,同时排除模棱两可的一对. 得到一个衡量标准支持的候选人在另一个方面可能仍然有重大错误,使单一衡量偏好可能不完整[11、4]。 第二,直接
偏好优化 (DPO) [20] 优化了相对偏好差异,但没有明确保留绝对合成忠心. 因此,只进行DPO微调可能会将模型从其经过预先训练的CT到PET绘图转移. 第三,一个单一的CT条件可以产生多个有效的偏好对. 将所有配对作为独立训练样本超重条件,并采用更有效的组合,在优化期间激励条件平衡配对选择.

blocks.en:
To address these challenges, we propose MedicalDPO , a
preference-alignment framework for Brownian Bridge-based CT-to-PET synthesis.
Given a CT condition, MedicalDPO evaluates multiple generated PET candidates along spatial, structural, and intensity fidelity dimensions. Multi-dimensional ranking identifies high- and low-quality candidate pools, while strict cross-metric verification retains pairs with consistent quality separation across all fidelity measurements. Following Diffusion-DPO [ 27 ] , the resulting preference pairs are used to optimize relative policy-reference denoising errors under the Brownian Bridge process. The preference objective is jointly optimized with the original Brownian Bridge training objective to preserve absolute synthesis fidelity. For CT conditions associated with multiple valid pairs, MedicalDPO rotates one pair per condition across training epochs, exposing the model to diverse preference supervision while maintaining condition-level balance.

blocks.en: MedicalDPO is evaluated on two Brownian Bridge-based CT-to-PET models, BBDM [ 12 ] and the domain-guided CPDM [ 16 ] . Quantitative and qualitative results demonstrate improved synthesis quality across both backbones. The complementarity and quality separation of the constructed preference pairs are further examined, while ablation studies assess the effects of the original training objective and multi-pair rotation.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We formulate stochastic CT-to-PET refinement as intra-condition preference learning. Multiple PET candidates generated from the same CT expose a quality hierarchy that provides automatically available supervision, with candidate quality represented across complementary spatial, structural, and intensity dimensions. • We introduce a multi-objective preference construction strategy that combines multi-dimensional candidate ranking with strict cross-metric verification, retaining strict pairs with cross-metric-consistent quality separation. • We develop a stable preference adaptation framework for Brownian Bridge models by combining relative denoising-error preference optimization with the original training objective and condition-balanced multi-pair rotation. Experiments on BBDM and CPDM demonstrate improvements across perceptual, intensity, structural, and reconstruction metrics.

blocks.en: 2.1 CT-to-PET Translation
blocks.zh: 2.1 CT对PET 翻译

blocks.en:
Image-to-image (I2I) translation learns mappings between visual domains,
with paired approaches such as Pix2Pix [ 10 ] .
GAN-based methods have also been explored for CT-to-PET
translation [ 2 ] , but may suffer from training instability and
mode collapse [ 24 ] , motivating diffusion-based
alternatives [ 9 ] .
BBDM [ 12 ] formulates I2I translation as a Brownian Bridge
directly connecting the source and target domains, while
CPDM [ 16 ] adapts this framework to CT-to-PET synthesis using
domain-specific attention and attenuation guidance.
Despite strong performance, both are trained mainly with per-sample diffusion objectives and don’t explicitly use relative quality differences among stochastic PET candidates, motivating preference-based refinement.

blocks.en: 2.2 Preference Optimization for Diffusion Models
blocks.zh: 2.2 最佳传播模式

blocks.en:
Preference optimization provides a natural way to align generative
models with desired output characteristics. RLHF learns a reward model
from pairwise comparisons and optimizes it through reinforcement
learning [ 18 ] , whereas DPO [ 20 ] learns directly from
preferred and rejected samples without an explicit reward model.
For diffusion models, prior work has explored reinforcement-learning
reward maximization [ 3 , 6 ] and preference-based
optimization [ 27 , 14 ] . In particular,
Diffusion-DPO [ 27 ] adapts DPO to diffusion models using
pairwise preference data.
Existing diffusion preference methods mainly target general-purpose or
text-to-image generation, where preferences are commonly defined by
human judgments, visual appeal, or text-image alignment. Medical image
translation instead requires task-specific preferences that jointly
reflect spatial, intensity, and structural fidelity, motivating the
preference formulation developed in this work.

blocks.en: We evaluate MedicalDPO for CT-to-PET translation on two diffusion-based backbones, BBDM [ 12 ] and CPDM [ 16 ] , with Pix2Pix [ 10 ] included as a GAN-based baseline.

blocks.en: Quantitative Analysis. The proposed preference construction identifies higher-quality PET candidates by combining complementary fidelity measurements with cross-metric consistency. We first examine whether the selected metrics provide distinct ranking information for candidates from the same CT condition. blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We propose MedicalDPO, a preference-alignment framework for Brownian Bridge-based CT-to-PET synthesis. It builds reliable preference pairs covering spatial, structural, and intensity fidelity, and adapts denoising-error preference optimization to Brownian Bridge models via a trainable policy with a frozen reference. Multi-pair rotation and backbone-preserving regularization help balance preference learning with retention of pretrained generation behavior. Experiments on BBDM and CPDM show consistent gains across perceptual, intensity, structural, and reconstruction metrics, with analyses supporting preference reliability. Ablations confirm backbone-preserving regularization is critical to prevent the degradation seen with preference-only fine-tuning. Overall, the results suggest preference optimization can inject medical quality criteria into diffusion-based image translation. Limitations include 2D slice-based synthesis and mainly image-fidelity evaluation. Future work will extend to native 3D translation and clinically relevant endpoints (e.g., uptake quantification and lesion-level analysis), and study medically informed preference weighting, broader sensitivity analyses of preference construction, and sensitivity-aware fine-tuning.
blocks.zh: 我们提出医疗方案(MedicalDPO),作为以布朗桥为基础的CT到PET合成的偏好调整框架. 它构建了涵盖空间,结构,和强度忠贞的可靠偏好对子,并采用可被冻结的可训练政策,将去诺能-error偏好优化于布朗斯桥模型. 多 Pair旋转和保留骨干正规化有助于平衡偏好学习和保留预先训练的生成行为。 有关BBDM和CPDM的实验显示,在观念、强度、结构和重建度量度方面都取得了一致的进展,分析支持了偏好可靠性。 减值证实保留骨干正规化对于防止仅以优惠微调方式出现的退化至关重要。 总的来说,结果表明,优化偏好可以将医疗质量标准注入基于传播的图像翻译。 局限性包括以2D切片为主的合成,并主要进行图像真实性评价. 今后的工作将扩展到本地的三维翻译和临床相关终点(如吸收量化和损伤水平分析),并研究医学上知情的偏好权重、对偏好结构的更广泛的敏感性分析以及敏感度的微调。
